req.title: Posts include author username
req.statement: The system shall join post rows with users so index/detail responses include the author's username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET / joins post rows with users and returns the author's username in the response. Tests must verify: (1) positive — username appears in index HTML for known posts; (2) negative — a response without the JOIN would lack the username field; (3) boundary — the single-post edge case where exactly one post exists and its username is present. Additional tests cover multiple authors, exact username values from seed data, and the SQL JOIN semantics by checking specific username/title pairings. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact byte strings, exact status codes (200 not >=200), and both sides of the join (username present AND correct value).

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_returns_200_and_contains_author_username():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data

test_index_returns_200_and_contains_author_username()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_empty_db_returns_200_no_usernames():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
        init_db()
        db = get_db()
        db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
        db.execute('DELETE FROM user')
        db.commit()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    for name in [b'Rahul', b'Anjali', b'Ishaan', b'Diya', b'James']:
        assert name not in r.data

Insert exactly one user 'SoloUser' and one post authored by that user
Send GET /
Assert status 200

Assert b'OnlyTitle' in response

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash

def test_index_single_post_single_author_username_present():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
        init_db()
        db = get_db()
        db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
        db.execute('DELETE FROM user')
        db.execute('INSERT INTO user (id, username, password) VALUES (1, ?, ?)',
                   ('SoloUser', generate_password_hash('pw')))
        db.execute('INSERT INTO post (id, title, body, author_id) VALUES (1, ?, ?, 1)',
                   ('OnlyTitle', 'OnlyBody'))
        db.commit()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'SoloUser' in r.data
    assert b'OnlyTitle' in r.data

test_index_single_post_single_author_username_present()

tests.name: test_index_most_recent_post_author_james_appears_first_in_data
preconditions: Post id=20 created='2025-04-01 10:30:37' authored by Rahul (id=1) is most recent
Index orders posts by created DESC
actions: Create app with test config and temp DB
Send GET /
Assert status 200
Assert b'Heacon signal pulse' (title of post 20) in response
Assert b'Rahul' appears in response (author of most recent post)
Assert position of 'Heacon signal pulse' before 'Pulse ember signal' in raw bytes
expected: Most recent post title appears before older post title in response
trace: R-FLASKR-024: JOIN result ordered DESC by created; most recent post's author shown first
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_most_recent_post_author_james_appears_first_in_data():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.data
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in data
    assert b'Rahul' in data
    idx_recent = data.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')
    idx_older = data.find(b'Pulse ember signal')
    assert idx_recent != -1
    assert idx_older != -1
    assert idx_recent < idx_older

test_index_most_recent_post_author_james_appears_first_in_data()
